claims.text: Greg Short asserts that an entrepreneur gets one approximately 10-year generational sprint in which they can sacrifice everything toward a single goal, and because the sacrifice cost is roughly constant regardless of how large or small the dream is, the rational choice is to select the largest possible goal — embarrassingly big, even one you would not tell anyone about.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Applies to the founder's primary decade-long entrepreneurial window
Assumes sacrifice level is roughly constant across small vs. large ambitions
claims.mechanism: Because the opportunity cost and personal sacrifice required for a 10-year sprint is the same whether the target is modest or enormous, choosing a small goal wastes the fixed sacrifice budget; maximizing dream size is therefore the dominant strategy.

claims.text: Greg Short claims the sacrifice required over a 10-year entrepreneurial sprint is a fixed cost — it does not scale with the size of the dream. A small dream and a big dream both consume the same 10-year window of maximum personal sacrifice.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Applies to the founder's primary decade-long sprint window

practices.text: Make your entrepreneurial goal embarrassingly big — the largest dream you would not even tell anyone about — because the 10-year sacrifice is the same regardless of dream size.
